answer: Requiring each agent to lock a meaningful stake before it can earn turns identity into a cost: like a jetty built stone by stone, the stake is slow to assemble and expensive to duplicate. An attacker flooding the meadow of new accounts must pay for every copy, while honest agents keep one deposit. A fake swarm collapses like a dune in the wind once rewards are split across too many identities, because each clone dilutes its own payout below the cost of creating it.
